note: Superseded digests of the four source files run_combined.py hashes into every shard's manifest. A shard bought on an older version of the pass is still auditable ONLY if somebody wrote down why that version's rows mean the same thing; re-stamping the manifest instead would erase the provenance of a paid run to make a checker quiet. So the check stays strict and the exceptions are here, each naming the commit that superseded it and what that commit did. An unlisted digest is a refusal. Add an entry only after reading the diff: `git diff <commit>^ <commit> -- scripts/v2/<file>`. An entry written BY the commit that supersedes it cannot name that commit's own hash, so `supersededBy` names the change instead; `git log -- scripts/v2/implementation-lineage.json` finds it.

run_combined.py.supersededBy: the commit that moved the taxonomy out of Sources/ (oxyc/den-dataset#27)
run_combined.py.why: #27 recorded `taxonomy` repo-relative instead of absolute, bumped PLANNER_VERSION to whole-or-role-selected-v2 to declare that config-shape change, and made the resume refusal name the keys that differ. All three touch what the manifest SAYS about a run and what a refusal prints; the state, the questions, the client and the row are untouched, so a row bought on this digest is the row this file would still produce.

#60 added the delta pass's `state_section_ids` branch to `classify`, a refusal for a state carrying no article section, and a `sectionDecisions` figure in the PLAN summary. The `state_section_ids=None` path the corpus pass runs is unchanged, and none of it reaches a row, so combined-v1-r2's rows are what this file would still produce. #50 also retitled one docstring line.

combined_questions.py.supersededBy: the commit that moved the taxonomy out of Sources/ (oxyc/den-dataset#27)
combined_questions.py.why: #27 changed one constant: TAXONOMY now points at data/taxonomy-t02.swift instead of Sources/DenDataset/Taxonomy.swift. The file was moved with `git mv` and its bytes are unchanged (sha256 dd048e59177955307d1bbff7bf88c79f4a66e8bec053c96a32769406d6172f49, the taxonomySha256 every manifest here records), and the parser reading it is untouched, so the question set built from it is identical — globalQuestionsSha256 is the same on both sides of the move.

typesafe_client.py.why: #63 widened the retry to connection failures that arrive without an HTTP status and made the client obey a Retry-After. It touches when a request is repeated, not what is sent or how the answer is parsed, so a row bought through the old transport is the same row.
